name: Clay Higgins
signature: Calls AI an 'Armageddon level threat' in government hands, pushes bills to bar AI-run IRS audits and AI-generated comment floods, and says the states are a fitting 'petri dish' for AI rules.

notable_quote.text: AI is an Armageddon level threat, far more ominous than any alleged pandemic or climate crisis,

data_centers.summary: No public statements found on data centers, Meta's Richland Parish project, or electricity bills as of Sept 2026. He voted for the SPEED Act in Dec 2025, which speeds federal permits for energy and infrastructure projects in general but does not mention data centers.

evidence.title: Press release: Higgins votes for the SPEED Act permitting bill
evidence.quote: The SPEED Act cuts red tape, streamlines permitting, and provides certainty for new projects. We're getting the federal government out of the way and allowing American workers to move forward on projects that grow the economy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He favors faster federal permitting for energy and industrial projects generally, but the statement says nothing about data centers or power bills.

ai_risk.summary: Higgins treats AI in government hands as a serious threat to liberty and has pushed bills to bar AI-selected IRS audits, AI enforcement of regulations, and AI-generated comment floods in rulemaking. His concern is government misuse and fake content, not safety rules for AI companies.

evidence.title: Press release: Higgins to introduce bill banning government weaponization of AI
evidence.quote: AI is an Armageddon level threat, far more ominous than any alleged pandemic or climate crisis,
evidence.what_it_shows: He uses alarming language about AI but aims his bill at stopping federal agencies from using AI to enforce laws, not at AI developers.

evidence.title: Press release: Higgins and Burlison introduce the No AI Audits Act
evidence.quote: We, as a Congress who have been sworn to serve the people, must think seriously about the implications of the rapid deployment of AI technology.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a human IRS investigator, not AI, to pick audits and calls for a GAO review of IRS AI use.

evidence.title: Press release: Higgins secures AI policy wins in Oversight Committee markup
evidence.quote: AI is being rapidly deployed throughout our federal government as a tool to enforce laws, regulations, and codes without regard to the severe risks,
evidence.what_it_shows: His language requiring a human review appeals process for government AI decisions was added to a bipartisan federal AI package.

evidence.title: Press release: Higgins reintroduces H.R. 9643, the Comment Integrity and Management Act
evidence.quote: As AI and other technologies advance, it is important that we preserve the integrity of constituent interactions. This legislation will ensure that Americans' voices are not drowned out by automated content generated by bad actors.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants agencies to verify that public comments come from humans, a targeted rule against AI-generated comment floods; the House passed an earlier version in May 2024.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: TAKE IT DOWN Act (H.R. 633), criminalizing AI-faked sexual images
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the main federal law against non-consensual and AI-faked intimate images.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Federal A.I. Governance and Transparency Act of 2024 (H.R. 7532)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported making agencies track and disclose the AI they use.

tech_regulation.summary: Mixed. He backed bills to stop federal officials from pressuring platforms to remove posts and to crack down on TikTok and Chinese drones, then in 2025 demanded social media CEOs ban users for life over posts celebrating Charlie Kirk's killing. He was recorded as not voting on the House KIDS Act in June 2026.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Protecting Speech from Government Interference Act (H.R. 140)
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to bar federal workers from pressuring social media companies to take down posts.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: ACES Act of 2023 (H.R. 4927) targeting TikTok and Chinese apps
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports restricting Chinese-controlled social media apps over spying concerns.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Countering CCP Drones Act (H.R. 2864)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs cutting Chinese drone maker DJI off from US airwaves.

evidence.title: Press release: Higgins' second letter to social media executives on posts celebrating Charlie Kirk's assassination
evidence.quote: Repeat offenders should absolutely not be allowed to remain on your platforms and post celebration of death.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed platforms to remove and permanently ban users, a demand for tougher content policing that sits uneasily with his anti-censorship bills.

evidence.title: House Vote #228: H.R. 7757, the KIDS Act (kids' online safety package), recorded as Not Voting
evidence.what_it_shows: He did not cast a vote when the House passed its kids' online safety package.

preemption.summary: After Trump's Dec 2025 executive order targeting state AI laws, Higgins told NOTUS he does not care about the politics and that the states are a good testing ground for how to handle AI. That leans against federal preemption, though he has not cosponsored a bill on it.

evidence.title: NOTUS: Will Trump's AI agenda backfire? Higgins on state AI laws after the executive order
evidence.quote: I think the sovereign states are an appropriate sort of petri dish for what AI might be. They are a good place for that mix to see, which may develop in the space where AI intersects our life.
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked about the executive order aimed at state AI laws, he said states should be able to experiment with AI rules, which cuts against a federal moratorium.

china_chips.summary: No statements found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China. His China-tech record covers TikTok and DJI drones, not semiconductors.

name: Mike Johnson
signature: Speaker who pledged to 'regulate only where we must' on AI, wants one national framework over state laws, and calls a data center moratorium 'a dangerous prospect'.
groups: Established the House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence with Leader Jeffries (Feb 2024)
House Republican leadership joint statement committing to enact the White House national AI framework (Mar 20, 2026)

notable_quote.text: America will win the AI race. We will win it if two things happen, if government resists the siren song of control and if industry steps up as our patriotic partner.

data_centers.summary: Johnson frames data centers as essential to beating China in AI, opposes a federal moratorium, and wants faster permitting and more gas, nuclear and coal power to run them. Under pressure from vulnerable Republicans, his office scheduled a September 2026 House vote on a bipartisan bill to keep data center power costs off household bills.

evidence.title: Michigan Advance (via Livingston Post): Johnson rejects a data center moratorium while campaigning in Lansing
evidence.quote: We're in a race with China on that AI race, and if they're able to leapfrog us in that race, it's a very dangerous thing for everybody around the country,
evidence.what_it_shows: He called a broad moratorium on data centers 'kind of a dangerous prospect right now' while saying companies should work with local officials and take community concerns into account.

evidence.title: KTIV interview in Sioux City: Johnson on data centers and AI
evidence.quote: Data centers are directly related to that. We have to fuel AI because we have to keep our edge.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pushed back on community opposition to data centers and said China is spreading misinformation to turn communities against them.

evidence.title: Speech: Speaker Johnson at the Hill and Valley Forum, 'America Will Win the AI Race'
evidence.quote: We all know the amount of energy required to power all these data centers and meet our national demands is truly enormous.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called for more natural gas, oil, nuclear and coal, streamlined permitting, and asked tech companies to build data centers and chips on American soil.

evidence.title: Benzinga (via TradingView): Speaker's office confirms House vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.quote: The bill will be on the floor of the House next week,
evidence.what_it_shows: His spokesperson Taylor Haulsee confirmed a floor vote on a bipartisan bill asking state regulators to make data centers cover costs of new power they need, a modest ratepayer step after months of pressure.

ai_risk.summary: Johnson's stated approach is to 'simplify and streamline where we can, regulate only where we must' so America wins the AI race with China. He created a bipartisan House AI task force in 2024 to weigh guardrails and says a national framework should protect kids, but as of Sept 2026 he had not answered House Democrats' call to cancel recess and pass safeguards against catastrophic AI risks.

evidence.title: Speech: Speaker Johnson at the Hill and Valley Forum, 'America Will Win the AI Race'
evidence.quote: this is our commitment in a simple summary: simplify and streamline where we can, regulate only where we must, and pave the way for American dominance.
evidence.what_it_shows: His governing philosophy for AI is light-touch: speed, streamlining, and minimal new rules, with government urged to resist 'the siren song of control'.

evidence.title: Press release: House launches Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence
evidence.quote: to explore how Congress can ensure America continues to lead the world in AI innovation while considering guardrails that may be appropriate to safeguard the nation against current and emerging threats.
evidence.what_it_shows: With Leader Jeffries he created a 24-member task force whose December 2024 report weighed both innovation and guardrails.

evidence.title: Nola.com: Louisiana waits to see how Trump, Congress will regulate AI (Johnson's office on the Kill Switch bill)
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked whether he would back a bipartisan bill letting DHS order shutdown of dangerous AI systems, his spokesperson did not answer and pointed to his 'regulate only where we must' remarks.

evidence.title: CNN: House Democrats urge Speaker Johnson to cancel recess to pass AI safeguards, citing 'catastrophic' risk
evidence.what_it_shows: Reps. Liccardo, Whitesides, Trahan and Lieu asked him to keep the House in session for AI safeguards against cyber and bioweapon risks; no response from him was reported.

tech_regulation.summary: Mixed. In Dec 2024 Johnson stalled the Senate-passed Kids Online Safety Act over free speech and censorship worries, then in June 2026 the House passed a narrower KIDS Act that he praised as holding Big Tech accountable. He also backed a bill barring officials from pressuring platforms to remove posts.

evidence.title: Fox News: Speaker Johnson says 'still some concern' about the Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.quote: There's still some concern about the free speech components of that, and whether it might lead to further censorship by the government of valid, you know, conservative voices, for example.
evidence.what_it_shows: He declined to bring the Senate's 91-3 KOSA to a House vote in 2024, citing censorship fears and FTC power.

evidence.title: Roll Call: House online safety bills take narrower approach than Senate
evidence.quote: I've talked to the leaders, the authors of the previous bill, about concerns that were expressed and that they work to address that. So I hope and assume that they have.
evidence.what_it_shows: He signaled openness to a House kids' safety package once his earlier objections to KOSA were addressed.

evidence.title: Press release: House passes KIDS Act to protect children, teens online
evidence.quote: This legislation represents an important step forward in Congress' effort to protect children online and hold big tech accountable, while also empowering parents and protecting free speech,
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the narrower House kids' online safety bill (H.R. 7757) and framed it as accountability for Big Tech balanced with free speech.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Free Speech Protection Act (H.R. 4791)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported barring government officials from pressuring platforms to take down posts, an anti-censorship rather than anti-Big-Tech measure.

preemption.summary: Johnson wants one national AI framework that 'avoids a patchwork of state regulations' and, with other House GOP leaders, pledged to enact the White House framework that calls for preempting state AI laws. Eighty-one House Democrats wrote to him in Nov 2025 opposing any revival of the state-law moratorium in the defense bill.

evidence.title: Joint statement: Johnson, Scalise, Guthrie, Jordan, Babin pledge to implement the national AI framework
evidence.quote: Today, the Trump Administration took a critical step in releasing a framework that gives Congress a roadmap to pursue legislation that provides innovators with much-needed certainty, while protecting consumers and prioritizing kids' online safety.
evidence.what_it_shows: House GOP leadership endorsed the White House framework, which calls for blocking state AI laws that impose 'undue burdens' in favor of a single national standard.

evidence.title: Speech: Speaker Johnson at the Hill and Valley Forum
evidence.quote: The first thing is we have to deliver a single national framework that protects children, safeguards communities, supports creators, and avoids a patchwork of state regulations.
evidence.what_it_shows: He listed replacing state-by-state AI rules with one federal framework as Congress's first AI job.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats to Speaker Johnson and other leaders opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and by executive order
evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
evidence.what_it_shows: He was the lead recipient of the Democratic letter fighting the push to put a state AI law moratorium into the defense bill; the moratorium was left out of the final NDAA.

china_chips.summary: Johnson calls China an adversary that steals intellectual property and says the American AI stack should reach allies while staying out of adversaries' hands, but he has taken no public stand found on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales or on specific export control bills. He voted against the 2022 CHIPS Act and briefly floated repealing it in 2024.

evidence.title: CNBC Squawk Box: Johnson says China is straining U.S. relations with Nvidia chip ban
evidence.quote: They have no regard whatsoever for U.S. trademark law or any of the other provisions that make for fair trade agreements. It is not the fault of the United States that there are these strained relations.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called China an 'adversary' after Beijing told firms to stop buying Nvidia chips, hawkish rhetoric without a stated position on US export limits.

evidence.title: Speech: Speaker Johnson at the Hill and Valley Forum
evidence.quote: And we know it's possible to expand the American AI stack to friends and allies, while also ensuring it stays out of the hands of America's adversaries and rivals.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs exporting American AI to allies while keeping it from China, the administration's framing that supports both sales abroad and controls on adversaries.

evidence.title: Bloomberg via SCMP: Johnson floats, then walks back, repeal of the CHIPS and Science Act
evidence.quote: I expect that we probably will, but we haven't developed that part of the agenda yet.
evidence.what_it_shows: He had voted against the chip-factory subsidy law and suggested repeal before saying it was 'not on the agenda for repeal'.

name: Julia Letlow
signature: Chief cheerleader for Meta's $50 billion Richland Parish data center, now the Trump-backed GOP Senate nominee with AI super PAC support; condemned an AI deepfake attack video in her runoff.

notable_quote.text: I'm thrilled that Meta is committing to cover the full cost, protecting ratepayers while supporting our local businesses, education, and infrastructure.

data_centers.summary: Letlow has championed Meta's Hyperion data center in her district since its 2024 launch, calling the $50 billion expansion 'transformative' and 'responsible growth' and praising Meta's promise to cover energy and water costs so ratepayers are protected. Reporting in Aug 2026 showed she signed a Meta NDA in June 2024, before the project was public, and later bought Meta and Nvidia stock that she disclosed late.

evidence.title: Press release: Letlow statement on Meta expansion in Northeast Louisiana
evidence.quote: I'm thrilled that Meta is committing to cover the full cost, protecting ratepayers while supporting our local businesses, education, and infrastructure. After years of our children moving away, responsible growth is on the horizon
evidence.what_it_shows: She celebrates the project and treats Meta's voluntary pledge to pay for energy, water and infrastructure as sufficient ratepayer protection, without asking for new conditions.

evidence.title: WWNO/Gulf States Newsroom: Letlow's remarks at Meta's Dec 2024 launch event
evidence.quote: I was so excited about it, I even skipped a vote in Washington. Don't tell anybody, please.
evidence.what_it_shows: She skipped a House vote to attend the public launch of the Richland Parish data center and cheered it on.

evidence.title: KNOE: Letlow addresses budget bill and Meta data center at Monroe luncheon

evidence.title: WWNO investigation: Letlow signed a Meta NDA on June 29, 2024, then bought Meta and Nvidia stock disclosed late

ai_risk.summary: Her only AI-safety-type actions are on deepfakes: she cosponsored the DEFIANCE Act in Jan 2026 and in June 2026 demanded her Senate rival take down an AI parody video of her, calling it 'disgraceful and indefensible.' At the same time the AI industry super PAC Leading the Future endorsed her and its Republican arm spent for her, and she has taken no public stand found on broader AI rules.

evidence.title: Breitbart: Leading the Future super PAC expands House GOP endorsements, including Letlow
